translationRepairs: In year 2, the empress dowager established her brother's son Marquis Lü Tai of Lü as King of Lü, carving out Jinan commandery from Qi as the King of Lü's fief.
In year 2, the empress dowager established her brother's son Lü Tai, the Marquis of Li, as King of Lü, carving out Jinan commandery from Qi as the King of Lü's fief.
酈侯 is Lü Tai's marquisate, the Marquis of Li; it is not part of his personal name.
In King Ai's third year, his younger brother Zhang entered Han's palace guard service. Empress Lü enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhuxu and married him to Lü Lü's daughter.
In King Ai's third year, his younger brother Zhang entered Han's palace guard service. Empress Lü enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhuxu and married him to Lü Lu's daughter.
呂祿 is Lü Lu; the first Lü is the surname and 祿 is Lu.
King Lü Lü of Zhao served as supreme general, King Lü Chan of Lü served as chancellor. Both resided in Chang'an, gathered troops to intimidate the ministers, and wished to rebel.
King Lü Lu of Zhao served as supreme general; King Lü Chan of Lü served as chancellor. Both resided in Chang'an, gathered troops to intimidate the ministers, and wished to rebel.
呂祿 is Lü Lu, not Lü Lü.
Lü Lü and Lü Chan wished to rebel in Guanzhong. Marquis Zhuxu together with Grand Marshal Bo and Chancellor Chen and others executed them.
Lü Lu and Lü Chan plotted rebellion within the passes, but the Marquis of Zhuxu, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, Chancellor Chen Ping, and their allies put them to death.
太尉勃 and 丞相平 are Grand Commandant Zhou Bo and Chancellor Chen Ping; the old literal text misnames both men.

The generals of the three kingdoms seized the Chamberlain and forced him to swear an oath, saying, "If you falsely report that Han has been defeated and urge Qi to surrender to us at once, Qi will soon be slaughtered."

The generals of the three kingdoms seized Palace Grandee Lu and forced him to swear an oath, saying, "When you return, say that Han has already been defeated and that Qi should quickly surrender to the three kingdoms. If you do not, you will be killed."
若反言 means 'when you return, say,' and 不且見屠 supplies the threatened consequence if Palace Grandee Lu refuses.
He reigned for a total of thirty-three years and died. His son Yan succeeded him and became King Qing.
After a total reign of thirty-three years, he died. His son Yan succeeded him as King Qing.
The successor is Liu Yan; 建 is source apparatus, not an additional part of his personal name.
He sent Marquis Jipu Chai as general to attack and defeat, capturing the King of Jibei. The king committed suicide, and the territory reverted to Han, becoming a commandery.
He sent General Chai, the Marquis of Jipu, who defeated and captured the King of Jibei. The king committed suicide, and the territory reverted to Han as a commandery.
棘蒲侯柴將軍 identifies General Chai as the Marquis of Jipu; the revised word order is clear and grammatical.
The King of Qi dispatched the Chamberlain for the Capital to carry word to the Son of Heaven.
The King of Qi sent Palace Grandee Lu to carry word to the Son of Heaven.
路 is the envoy's surname and 中大夫 his office; the old translation treated the whole expression as an office title.
The Son of Heaven instructed the Chamberlain to return to Qi with this message: 'Hold fast in your defense. My armies have now defeated Wu and Chu.'
The Son of Heaven instructed Palace Grandee Lu to return to Qi with this message: 'Hold fast in your defense. My armies have now defeated Wu and Chu.'
路中大夫 again names Palace Grandee Lu, the envoy returning from the Han court.
